challenge: Victoria Crater steep rim climb through a loose boulder field (Gen 0 edge: 0.28 m rocks)

challenge_spec.title: Victoria Crater steep rim climb through a loose boulder field (Gen 0 edge: 0.28 m rocks)
assumptions: Terrain: real elevation data, Victoria Crater (Opportunity), Mars (U01 uncontrolled) (80 m square, 5.3 m of relief, typical slope 9.5°). Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona HiRISE DTM.
Gravity set to 3.71 m/s² for mars.
Friction set to 0.7 for a regolith surface.
Loose regolith friction is set to 0.65 (calibration range 0.45–0.65); 12 path rocks are 0.20 m high (calibration range 0.15–0.35 m).
Must fit the lander: ≤ 12 kg, ≤ 0.8 × 0.5 m.
Escalated after a verified generation-zero design failed with approximately 0.28 m rocks.

results.name: Max-radius scout
results.reason: G0-B reached 100% in 20.0s at (-33.505,10.827) on 5.0deg slope; using its 0.02m length headroom for a larger wheel should ease rock rollover while staying stowed-legal.

results.name: Stable hexapod
results.reason: G0-C flipped at 26.8% at (-28.197,21.198) on 4.6deg slope; shorter legs and narrower stride should lower instability from its 0.38m legs and 22deg stride.

results.reason: G1-B stuck at 54.5% at (-33.488,10.722) on 5.0deg slope despite wider wheels, so six 0.20m wheels enlarge the contact patch and rollover using only its 0.02m length headroom.

verification.message: Light six-wheel rover reaches the goal 1 of 5 times (passes 1/5 (95% CI 4–62%)).
